records.name: Kırşehir
records.current_summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): central Anatolia. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 October 2025): a leaked draft omnibus reform (the '11th Judicial Package') would amend the penal code so that acting 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' — or its promotion — carries up to three years in prison (an amendment to article 225 on 'indecent acts'), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under onerous eligibility rules, and allow criminal charges against trans people and the professionals who treat them; justified as protecting 'the family' and 'public morals'. HRW called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks of the decade and urged withdrawal.

Kaos GL (24 February 2026): presentation of its 'LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025', titled 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People'. Findings: anti-LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — targeting of LGBTI+ people as 'deviant' or 'a threat' by the president and senior officials raised officials' motivation and third-party impunity; the new Family Ministry became the implementing ministry; one LGBTI+ rights organisation was closed; platforms and broadcasters were penalised or withdrew; artistic events were cancelled. The report documents six violations of the right to life (three hate-motivated killings; trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 the previous year, largely during assemblies) and 313 liberty violations in 2025 (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions). No official hate-crime statistics exist; cases rely on media.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (only site navigation was retrieved); the underlying bianet article (31 July 2025) covers about 20 trans women in the Beyoğlu district rounded up for identity checks at a police station — names recorded, videos filmed, no official reason given — the research dossier's '31 July 2025 mass ID roundups'.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
sources.claim: National-framework reference that governs this region record under rule 1, since Kırşehir stands under Turkey's state law. Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence since the Ottoman Empire adopted a new penal code in 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender (after surgery) since 1988. However, Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military, and same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition (no marriage, civil union, or adoption). Authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years since 2015, using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants; in ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking Turkey placed 47th out of 49 assessed countries. For this record: the legal protections a trans or LGBTQ visitor has (or lacks) are set entirely by this national framework, complementing the existing HRW, Kaos GL and Bianet sources already on the record.

records.name: Kocaeli
records.current_summary:
A trans visitor in Kocaeli is subject to the same nationwide developments as anywhere else in the country. An October 2025 leaked omnibus draft would amend the penal code to imprison acts deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality (up to three years; up to four for same-sex ceremonies), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, and expose doctors to up to seven years in prison; national monitoring reports that 2025 hostility became explicit state policy — family-year directives from the head of state, a rights organisation closed, broadcast and arts-event censorship, three hate-motivated killings, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations and a 2.5-fold rise in detentions.

No statute, incident or court case specific to Kocaeli appears in the surviving sources for this record: the documents behind it are national-level and carry no provincial breakdown. The absence of province-specific documentation is not evidence of local tolerance — the nationwide framework and its 2025-26 escalation reach this province as any other.

sources.claim: National-framework source (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): HRW news release, Oct 29, 2025, reports a leaked omnibus draft ("11th Judicial Package") that would amend the penal code to criminalise conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality with up to three years' prison, participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with up to four years, and would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals; healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and trans people receiving deemed-illegal care up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft; HRW warns it would force treatment underground and expose people to arrest and pretrial detention.

National-framework monitoring report (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): Kaos GL's 2025 review finds hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit state policy — "Year of the Family" instructions issued to public institutions, an LGBTI+ association closed with criminal cases against 11 of its members, and artistic events cancelled or banned. The report documents 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings (trans people the most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51 the prior year), roughly 313 total violations overall — about 2.5 times the previous year — with 299 detention decisions, and freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch (29 October 2025): a leaked draft judicial-reform package (the 11th Judicial Reform) would pave the way for criminal charges against LGBT people, described as one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades; activists held a press conference in Istanbul on 28 October 2025 against the provisions targeting LGBT people.

sources.title: LGBT rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
sources.claim: National-framework page for the law Muş province (like every Turkish province) stands under; no Muş-specific ordinance, incident or court decision was locatable in this pass, so this framework is the documented picture. Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, but there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. Openly LGBTI people are barred from serving in the military: conscripts who declare their homosexuality are classed under a definition of homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness', must provide photographic proof, and risk their 'unfit report' leaking publicly. Same-sex marriage is not recognised, and since 2015 local authorities have repeatedly banned and forcibly dispersed Pride marches (police used water cannon and tear gas on the 2015 and 2016 Istanbul parades). The page records early-2026 press reports that the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex', a provision that was ultimately not included in the year's judicial reform package.

sources.title: Türkiye - Amnesty International country report (Report 2025/26)
sources.claim: Amnesty International's Türkiye country report (Report 2025/26) documents the national LGBTI climate under which Muş province sits: in June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the Istanbul LGBTI and Trans pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force, over 90 people were arbitrarily detained, and prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end. In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling it had shared 'obscene' images incompatible with 'society's moral values' that could 'encourage or promote' LGBTI identities. Amnesty also records that three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people were made public during 2025 - an unprecedented assault that would criminalize expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible - but they were ultimately not submitted to parliament.

records.name: Ordu
records.current_summary:
No province-specific measure, incident or institution concerning transgender visitors is documented here in this edition's audited sources: what governs a trans visitor is the national picture, and no local authority is recorded adding bans or enforcement programs of its own.

The national framework as documented: a draft judicial package leaked in October 2025 would carry terms up to three years for conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality, up to four for same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies, raise the gender-care age floor to twenty-five with mandatory infertility conditions, and remove civil-status recognition of gender change. Ordu is a Black Sea province. Absence of provincial documentation describes the record, not a guarantee: national directives reach every province's institutions, and the assembly-ban and violence patterns were logged countrywide rather than per province.
